title: Combining customs and court remedies against counterfeit goods
p1:
A fake product entering the market is not just a sales problem — it can become a brand survival problem.

Many businesses think a court case is the only way to fight counterfeits. But there is another powerful step that often gets overlooked.
p2:
The surprising part? Stopping fake goods at the border can sometimes be faster than chasing them after they reach customers. Customs authorities may help block suspicious shipments before they enter the market.

But customs action and court remedies serve different purposes.
p3:
Customs measures focus on preventing counterfeit goods from coming in. Court remedies can help businesses seek damages, injunctions, and other legal protections after infringement occurs.

Using both together creates a stronger strategy: stop the damage early while also protecting your legal rights. The practical lesson for businesses is simple — enforcement works best when prevention and legal action move together.
conclusion: Have you seen a business rely only on court action while ignoring border protection against counterfeit goods?
